statement: The split abort path reaches merge's fencing parity: the split abort step result carries the claim fenceToken/ownerId so the abort transition persists through the fenced persistWorkflowTransition (today it persists unfenced with fenceToken: null while cutover and phase-advance paths are stamped), and the owner-recorded dissolution acks on the abort path are fence-stamped — a cross-process abort can never interleave with a fenced cutover through the unfenced abort write. doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/split-abort-fence-parity.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — abort-transition-fenced, abort-dissolution-acks-fenced, and cross-process-abort-cutover-exclusion receipts all passing.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
Each new regression test must fail when the corresponding mechanism is reverted while the rest of the change remains.
The oracle evidence files must be written by a deterministic evidence harness that re-runs the recorded proof commands (focused test files, red-on-revert probes) and writes the receipt artifact.

No owner-lane transition write may bypass assertTransitionFence (F18 residual): the abort path is the last unfenced split transition; cross-process protection must not rest on status re-validation alone.
